scope: New benchmark using the only handed-over code; candidate speed labels retained; not exact historical-figure restoration.
execution: Apply returned first control iff finite, even when SLSQP reports failure; no clipping or safety override. Finite entire SQP sequences are committed for original warm-start shifting. Nonfinite first control or exception is retained and stops that run.
obstacle_clock: Each cycle obstacles are recomputed from frozen initial states and absolute plan_time_s; no cumulative obstacle integration drift.
target_speed: Each SQP cycle calls the original R preparation once; its member desired speed accumulates the original near-goal decay. AL retains original behavior.

timing.solver_wall_ms: Original R/AL: steady_clock around full native solve, including local preparation, nominal initialization, optimization, and native logging. SQP: sum of steady_clock original-R preparation plus perf_counter nominal/constraint initialization and minimize. Both exclude obstacle prediction, supplementary cost/residual evaluation, execution, commit and serialization.
timing.solve_time_ms: Exact alias of solver_wall_ms for plot compatibility.
timing.native_clock_ms: Original returned Solution internal clock field; not the comparison timer, AL placeholder zero.

constraints: Original R and AL preserve different hard/soft constraint enforcement; SQP uses exact R penalty objective and original geometric residual definitions, R fixed control envelope and predicted internal acceleration bounds; it does not emulate the R iteration-dependent first-speed trust interval.
threading: Methods run sequentially; native AL std::async preserved. OMP/BLAS environment limits do not imply AL single-thread execution.

environment.profiling: Measurement-only timers; native AL asynchronous workers and native R logging retained; per-iteration costs measured over actual inner-loop bodies. SQP core includes QP, BFGS and line-search bookkeeping.
